author: @ShalnevaE
text: Russians don't commit a genocide, I said sorry several times and that's enough, I may go to Vyshka one day but now I live in two European states where I've been citizen since early 2000s and which thankfully impose no obligation on me to like ukranians.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: Apart from that, I have no obligation to like ukraine, and it's bizarre for you to imply that I should.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: Just surprised how true to their reputation ukranians turn out to be: crooked & thievish.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: It was Russia's business because the majority of Donbas's population were ethnic Russians?

author: @ShalnevaE
text: I was provoked, I replied in a state of shock, I apologised.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: Yes, and there is absolutely no point in trying to convince them otherwise. You can give them all the facts, present all the receipts, they will still parrot what they choose to believe. And quite viciously at that.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: When we trace you to source, I suspect that a bedsit with 1 window in London's zone 4 is exactly where we'll find you exercising your patriotism while dodging the ukranian draft. And it will be the bedsit I pay for with my additional-rate UK taxes. You don't get to tell me where to live, scum. And you are absolutely inane if you think that the UK, of which I am a citizen, supports the corrupt, inconsequential, nazi-infested dump that Ukrane has become.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: I never supported the Ukranian war. I caught the back end of the Soviet era when we were all one country and I went to school with Ukranian kids. I am a quarter Ukranian. I never rejoiced at the Ukranian war casualties or the destruction of the Ukranian land. But it's posts like this that make me wonder why Russia does not spare one of its 1,800 active nuclear warheads to end the affair quickly & cleanly without any further risk to the lives of our boys.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: I was going to go easy as I remember the times when we were all one country and I went to school with Ukranian kids. But since you post vapid provocation, here you go. There is no "ignorance" of Ukranian culture as Ukranian culture practically doesn't exist. The language is a weak pastiche of Russian and doesn't render itself to literature of any note. While Russian authors have been studied at every university in the world and Russian music played at every concert hall in the world, even during the Cold War, Ukranian artists made no mark on the world at all. So no chauvinism, just fact. Georgia has a far more advanced culture that Ukrane, which I admit readily despite not liking where Georgia is heading politically. You should troll less.

author: @ShalnevaE
text: Unfair, but I'm glad we agree on the point of principle: Ukrane's "high culture" is one poet called Taras Shevchenko. His level was such that he never made it to a single university curriculum outside Ukrane.

author: @ShalnevaE
text:
Making the masses literate was a mistake, for they persistently fail to know their place.

The fact that they can read, i.e. understand signs on a page, doesn't mean that they understand what's written, i.e. "the essence of the world" expressed by the author. Yet they behave like they do and aggressively demand that others bend to their mindset. Through sheer multitudes, they win.

Also, for an "unlikable narrator", one should read Marquis de Sade. Not sure how Hemingway made the cut.
